battle.name: 灤水谷之戰
battle.brief: 開元二年夏秋之交，契丹首領大祚榮率部眾自營州南下寇邊。唐以幽州長史薛耽為主將，據灤水谷險隘設伏，步兵持長矛、拒馬列於谷口，弩手居高齊射覆蓋谷道，待契丹騎兵入谷難以展開，合擊兩翼、斷其歸路，斬首數千級。卡面這件埃及長矛早了三千年，是長柄刺擊兵器的祖型，唐軍對應者正是槊與長矛。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 開元二年（714）的灤水谷之戰，參戰的兩方是唐王朝與契丹。北方是唐玄宗李隆基治下的開元朝廷：最高決策在京城的中書門下與兵部，邊防部署則落在北邊重鎮之一的幽州（後稱范陽）軍府。唐在幽州一線設有幽州長史、營田使、防御使等職，長史兼領軍府，總攬州境城戍、屯田、戶口與烽堠之務；安東都護府則是唐在遼東方向的軍府，治所在營州（今遼寧朝陽一帶），負責羈縻奚、契丹、室韋等部族的羈縻與撫納，兼管彈壓、互市與叛逃之事。灤水谷位在幽州與營州之間的交通走廊上，控扼自營州通往關內的山海道與鹽、馬通道，因此由幽州軍府主持防禦，安東都護府居中策應，兩套體系在邊境上互相策應、互為犄角。契丹一方則是尚未建立中原式編制的部族聯盟：大祚榮為其大可汗，以牙帳為中樞，諸部首領各自領兵，既服從大可汗的號令，又保留本部畜牧、徵發與械鬥的方式；兵員以部落民為主，能夠迅速集結為大規模騎兵集群。史冊所謂『二十萬』，多為史官誇張之辭，實際出戰人數當在數萬之譜；此外契丹部眾向來不喜久攻，習慣深入抄掠、得手即返，因此此役屬邊境衝突而非決戰。戰後雙方的往來被記為契丹內附與唐廷屢加羈縻的關係，並非國家對國家的正式交涉。
countriesEn: The Battle of Lianshui Valley of 714 pits the Tang dynasty against the Khitan. On one side stands the Kaiyuan court of Emperor Xuanzong Li Longji: supreme direction lay with the chancellery and the Ministry of War in the capital, while the frontier deployment fell to the military prefecture of Youzhou, later called Fanyang, one of the northern garrison towns. Along the Youzhou line the Tang maintained the offices of military prefect, agricultural commissioner and defence commissioner; the military prefect also commanded the prefectural army, taking in hand the walled posts, the state farms, the registered households and the beacon towers of the province, while the Andong Protectorate, the Tang military office for the Liaodong direction, had its seat at Yingzhou, around modern Chaoyang in Liaoning, and was charged with holding the Xi, Khitan and Shiwei peoples in the loose jimi system of controlled tribes, as well as with policing, frontier trade and deserters. Lianshui Valley lay on the traffic corridor between Youzhou and Yingzhou, controlling the road that ran from Yingzhou into the passes beyond the Wall as well as the salt and horse routes, so the defence was led by the Youzhou military prefecture while the Andong Protectorate gave support from the rear; the two systems reinforced one another along the border. The Khitan side was as yet a tribal confederacy without a Chinese-style administrative apparatus: Dazuo Rong was their great khan, with the command tent as the centre of power, and the chiefs of the various tribes each led their own men, both obeying the great khan's orders and keeping their own ways of raising livestock, levies and fighters; the soldiers were drawn from the tribal population itself, were mostly mounted, and could be mustered quickly into large bodies of cavalry. The figure of 'two hundred thousand' in the books is the usual exaggeration of Tang frontier chroniclers; the actual force deployed was probably in the tens of thousands. The Khitan moreover had no taste for protracted fighting, being used to riding deep, plundering and returning, so this engagement was a border clash rather than a decisive battle. After it, the relations between the two sides are recorded as the Khitan submitting and the Tang repeatedly renewing their jimi arrangements, not a formal negotiation between two states.
people: 唐方的主將是薛耽。他是瓜州長史薛收一系的後人，隋末隨秦王入關，家族以文臣起家，薛耽卻以治邊著稱，歷官右武衛將軍，開元初年出為安東都護、幽州長史，兼領防御之任，長期坐鎮范陽，成為開元前期唐廷倚重的北方宿將。灤水谷之戰由他統籌：他一方面整肅營州至幽州的沿邊城戍與烽燧，另一方面組織步騎在河谷地形中設伏，以己方對地形的掌握去對沖契丹騎兵的機動力。與他同在軍府任事的還有營田使等屬官，掌屯田、糧秣與軍籍，供應遠征所需的草料；基層將校姓名多佚於史乘，僅知部將中多有契丹、奚、室韋的內附部眾充當向導與騎手。契丹方面的核心人物是大祚榮，姓李，唐人稱其為李大祚榮，契丹語名娭娭，各書音譯寫法不一，是契丹李氏部族的領袖，其祖父曾受唐廷封爵，到他手上仍以藩屬的名義向朝廷貢馬、請封。他這次南下寇邊，既是部族生存的擴張，也是對唐廷邊貿與羈縻待遇變化的直接反應；史籍同載契丹部首領李養直隨行，兩人分率本部。戰後大祚榮退回營州，次年（開元三年）病逝，其子咄吉嗣位。宰相層面，開元二年在位者為姚崇，年內由宋璟接任；二人對北方邊策的主張雖有緩急之別，但都主張厚積糧草、固守城防、不與契丹騎兵在平原上爭鋒，其取向與灤水谷之戰的實際打法互相呼應。
peopleEn: The Tang commander was Xue Dan. A descendant of the Xue family of Gaozhou, which had risen as literati under the Sui and entered the Tang with the Prince of Qin, Xue Dan himself made his name in frontier administration: he served as Right Imperial Guard general, and in the early Kaiyuan years was sent out as Andong Protector and then military prefect of Youzhou while also holding the defence portfolio, remaining for many years in command at Fanyang and becoming one of the northern veterans on whom the Kaiyuan court relied. The Battle of Lianshui Valley was his operation: on the one hand he tightened the walled posts and beacon towers along the line from Yingzhou to Youzhou, on the other he organised infantry and cavalry to lie in ambush among the river-valley terrain, using his mastery of the ground to cancel out the mobility of Khitan horsemen. Working with him in the military prefecture were the agricultural commissioner and other staff officers, who handled the state farms, the fodder, the grain and the military registers that sustained any distant operation; the names of the junior commanders are mostly lost, though among the troops were numbers of Khitan, Xi and Shiwei defectors and tributaries serving as guides and riders. The central figure on the Khitan side was Dazuo Rong, surnamed Li, called Li Dazuo Rong by the Chinese and known in Khitan as E'e, whose written form varies from book to book, leader of the Khitan Li clan; his grandfather had been enfeoffed with a title by the Tang, and even under Dazuo Rong the tribe still paid horses as tribute and petitioned for titles in the manner of a vassal. This descent on Youzhou was at once a tribal expansion and a direct answer to the change in the Tang court's frontier trade and jimi arrangements. The Khitan chief Li Yangzhi is recorded as accompanying him, the two leading separate contingents. After the war Dazuo Rong withdrew to Yingzhou and died of illness the following year, 715, his son Duoji succeeding him. At the level of the chancellery Yao Chong was in office in the second year of Kaiyuan and was replaced within the year by Song Jing. Their views on northern defence differed in emphasis, but both argued for accumulating grain, holding the fortified towns firmly and refusing to trade blows with Khitan cavalry on the open plain, an orientation that matches the actual conduct of the fighting at Lianshui Valley.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛，是早王朝時期的典型長柄兵器：銅或青銅矛頭以榫眼套合木杆，杆長及人肩胸之間，揮刺為主，亦可擲出。放在本役的時間軸上，它早了三千年有奇，只能算是長柄刺擊兵器的祖型；但正因為它奠定了『金屬矛頭加木杆』這個結構，後世所有長矛、槊都只是這一格式的放大與改進。在開元二年的幽州戰線上，與它功能對應的正是唐軍的槊與長矛：槊的矛頭多為鐵質，形制細長，裝於長杆，講究挺刺時不顫；步兵使用的長矛與盾相配，列陣時前排以矛牆攔截騎兵衝撞，後排以弩與弓補射；標槊則是可投擲的短柄矛，隨身攜帶，專用於擾亂與追擊。另外，唐軍的攻守裝備還有唐刀與環首刀、帶勾的長柄刀陌刀、弓箭與蹶張弩、床弩等攻城器械，配以皮甲、札甲、明光鎧等防護，以及護身的方盾與橢圓盾；騎兵則有馬甲與馬鎧，人甲一體的騎戰裝備。營地方面，唐軍在幽州、營州一線築有城障與烽燧，設木拒馬、鹿角與壕溝，專司遲滯敵騎；投石機、雲梯、攻城壕塹等器械在邊城攻守中亦常備。運輸依靠牛車與輜重車，糧秣以營田與軍倉供應，灤河與沽河一線的水運亦可分擔軍資。馬匹來源主要是北方牧場，契丹與奚的馬群是其騎兵戰力的根基。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card face is the typical long-handled weapon of the Early Dynastic period: a copper or bronze head socketed onto a wooden shaft, the shaft reaching to the shoulder or chest of the bearer, used chiefly for thrusting but also capable of being thrown. Set on the timeline of this campaign it is more than three thousand years early, so it can only serve as the ancestor type of the long-handled thrusting weapon; but precisely because it established the formula of a metal head joined to a wooden shaft, every later spear and sha was nothing more than an enlargement and refinement of the same pattern. On the Youzhou front in 714 the functional counterparts of that weapon were the Tang sha and the long spear: the head of a sha was generally of iron, slender in form and mounted on a long shaft, valued for not shaking when the thrust was made; the long spears carried by infantry were paired with shields, the front rank presenting a wall of spear-points to check the charge of horsemen while the rear ranks supplied covering fire with crossbows and bows; the biaoshao was a throwing spear with a short shaft, carried on the person, used for harassment and pursuit. The Tang armament also included the Tang dao and the ring-pommel sword, the long-handled dao with a hook, the miaodao, bows, the pedal crossbow and the bed crossbow used in siege work, together with leather armour, lamellar armour and the bright minguang mail, plus the rectangular and oval shields; the cavalry had chamfrons and horse armour, fighting in combined man-and-horse protection. On the defensive side the Tang maintained walls and beacon towers along the line from Youzhou to Yingzhou, with wooden cheval-de-frise, abatis and ditches laid out to delay the enemy horse, while stone-throwers, scaling ladders and siege ditches were also kept ready in the frontier towns. Transport depended on ox-carts and baggage wagons, with grain and fodder supplied from the state farms and the granaries of the region; the waterways of the Luan and the Gu could also carry part of the military traffic. Horses came mainly from the northern pastures, and the herds of the Khitan and the Xi were the foundation of the enemy's mounted strength.
tactics: 灤水谷的戰法，可由地形與雙方兵種的差異推知大概。契丹騎兵善於奔馳、散開、繞射與劫掠，最忌在狹窄的河谷中被堵死；唐軍則有步卒結陣與守險的傳統。開戰之前，幽州軍府先做的是清剿沿邊村邑、收攏牲畜，令敵騎無所掠奪，再把主力集中到谷口兩側的高地與坡地，砍伐樹木、堆積柴草，設置拒馬與鹿角，並在谷口狹窄處立拒馬槊、挖掘淺壕，以步兵持矛結成數層，弩手居高臨下分層齊射，弓手在後列覆蓋射界，騎兵則控扼谷口外的通道，準備截斷敵騎退路。待契丹騎兵湧入谷中，騎兵失去展開與縱馳的空間，唐軍即以弩箭覆蓋谷道，待其陣形散亂、前後不能相顧時全軍出擊：矛兵穩住正面，兩翼步騎同時合擊，把敵軍往谷內擠壓，切斷其與後隊的聯繫，截住歸路，迫其下馬步戰或倉皇突圍。追擊的界線則受制於糧秣與天氣，一旦超出供應範圍即收兵回塞，不作深入追擊。整條補給線是此役的關鍵：軍糧自幽州屯田與軍倉轉輸，車隊循渤海海岸的鹽道與山東道北上，灤水谷一線只是前沿的收容點；契丹那一方則靠騎兵掠奪與逐水草而戰，不依賴固定糧道，這正是其能短期集結數萬騎、又能在失利後迅速脫身的原因。
tacticsEn: The way the Battle of Lianshui Valley was fought can be reconstructed in outline from the terrain and from the difference between the two forces in kind. Khitan horsemen were good at galloping, deploying in loose order, shooting at an angle and carrying off plunder; what they least wanted was to be shut up in a narrow river valley. The Tang, by contrast, had the tradition of infantry forming up and holding the heights. Before the action, the Youzhou military prefecture first swept the villages along the frontier and drove off the cattle, so that the enemy horse would find nothing to seize; it then concentrated the main body on the heights and slopes on either side of the valley, felled trees and piled brushwood, set up cheval-de-frise and abatis, planted spear-tipped barriers and dug shallow ditches at the narrow mouth, formed the infantry into several ranks of spears, posted crossbowmen on the heights to shoot in volleys, put bows in the rear to cover the range of fire, and held the cavalry on the approaches outside the valley mouth ready to cut the enemy's line of retreat. Once the Khitan horsemen pressed into the valley and lost the room to deploy or to gallop, the Tang covered the track with crossbow fire, and, when the enemy's order had broken and front and rear could no longer support one another, the whole force went over to the attack: the spearmen stabilised the front, the two flanks closed in simultaneously, the enemy was pressed further into the valley, its contact with the rear cut off and its way back sealed, so that the Khitan had to fight on foot or break out in confusion. The limit of the pursuit was set by supply and by the weather: as soon as the troops moved beyond the reach of the supply line they withdrew to the fort and did not follow deep. The supply line was the crux of the operation. Military grain came from the state farms and granaries of Youzhou, the baggage trains moving north by the coastal salt road of the Bohai and by the Shandong circuits, while the Lianshui Valley line was only a forward collecting point. The Khitan, for their part, fought on captured supplies and on grazing, with no fixed line of supply to depend on, and that was precisely why they could concentrate tens of thousands of riders in a short time and yet slip away again quickly after a defeat.
data: 可考的數字並不多，且多出於史官的概括。《舊唐書》《新唐書》記契丹出動人數為『二十萬』，通鑑類編纂也沿用此數，這類數字在唐代邊患記載中普遍偏大，實際出戰的部落兵當在數萬之間，多為自備鞍馬、輕裝出擊的騎士。唐軍方面，幽州軍府是北方重鎮，轄城戍、屯田與民兵，開元年間常備兵數以萬計，但灤水谷一役的具體出動人數史無明文，諸家皆從略。戰果有比較具體的記載：斬首數千級，並俘獲一批部眾與馬匹。距離方面，灤水谷在幽州治所（范陽，今北京一帶）之東，經營州古道約五百里，契丹的營州根據地與幽州之間還夾著渝關、居庸關一線的山口，騎兵由營州南下到前線，單程約二百餘里，正好一日到兩日的行程，符合其晨發夕至、掠罄即返的用兵習慣。時間上，開元二年自春至秋都有北方警報，灤水谷之戰被記在夏秋之交；戰後至開元三年的一年間，契丹再度南下，張守珪於累支山擊破之，開元四年又擒其首領涅里，說明這場勝利並未一勞永逸地解決邊患。軍需方面，唐廷於開元前中期在河北、山東、關中推行屯田，邊州糧秣多可自給，僅鹽、馬、衣這三樣仍需從關內與江南調運，運量動以數十萬石計，是遠征得以維持的物質基礎。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are few, and most of them are the compressed generalisations of court chroniclers. The Old and New Tang Histories give the Khitan deployment as 'two hundred thousand', a figure the mirror-style compilers also carry over; numbers of this kind run high throughout Tang records of frontier trouble, and the warriors actually engaged were probably in the tens of thousands, for the most part lightly equipped riders with their own saddles and horses. On the Tang side the Youzhou military prefecture was a major northern garrison, holding walled posts, state farms and local levies, and in the Kaiyuan years it commonly kept a standing force counted in tens of thousands, but the number actually committed at Lianshui Valley is nowhere stated, every history passing over it. The results are recorded rather more concretely: several thousand heads cut off, together with a batch of captives and horses taken. As to distance, Lianshui Valley lay east of the seat of Youzhou at Fanyang, around modern Beijing, some five hundred li along the old Yingzhou road, and between the Khitan base at Yingzhou and Youzhou lay the passes of Yuzhou and Juyong; a rider coming south from Yingzhou had a little over two hundred li to cover, a day's to two days' journey, exactly in keeping with their habit of setting out in the morning, raiding and returning by night. In time, alarms from the north were recorded from spring through autumn of the second year of Kaiyuan, and the battle at Lianshui Valley is placed in the turn of summer and autumn; within the year that followed, the Khitan came south again and were broken by Zhang Shougui at Leizhi Mountain, and in the fourth year of Kaiyuan their chief Nieli was taken, which shows that the victory did not settle the frontier question once and for all. On supply, the Tang pushed state farming in Hopei, Shandong and Guanzhong in the early and middle Kaiyuan years, so the grain of the frontier prefectures could largely be grown locally; only salt, horses and cloth still had to be brought from the interior and from the south, in quantities measured in hundreds of thousands of hu, and that was the material basis on which any distant campaign was sustained.
cause: 此戰的近因在史籍中記載很簡略，舊新唐書只說契丹寇邊，沒有留下導火線的確切記載，諸說並存，但可以確定的是三件事。其一，契丹在隋唐之際完成了部族聯盟的重組，處於松漠與潢水之間的草場上，控制了奚、室韋等部，畜牧與馬群大量增加，能夠一次集結數萬騎兵，這是兵源與戰力的基礎。其二，開元初年唐廷對邊州的管理趨嚴，羈縻、互市、收馬與屯田的安排多有變動，契丹一方面依賴唐廷的市場與封爵，另一方面又因邊吏的貪索而積怨，一有風吹草動就以越境掠奪回應。其三，開元二年唐朝北方的整體局勢並未放鬆，草原上的勢力此消彼長，契丹試探性南進，試圖在邊防空隙中取得糧草、牛馬與人口。從大祚榮的處境看，這次出動帶有明顯的試探性質：他不求攻取城池，只求在邊緣地帶取勝；因此當唐軍在谷地設伏、居高臨下地打散他的騎兵鋒芒時，契丹沒有戀戰，立刻收攏人馬退回營州方向。營州都督府一線的情報與烽火傳遞，是唐軍得以提前在灤水谷佈防的直接條件；史家多強調，正是由於唐軍事先得到消息並結合了河谷地形，才讓一場本可能蔓延的邊患化為一次短促的決定性戰鬥。
causeEn: The immediate cause of this war is recorded very briefly in the histories. The Old and New Tang Histories say only that the Khitan raided the border and leave no trace of a specific spark; several explanations current, but three things can be established with certainty. First, the Khitan completed the reorganisation of their tribal alliance in the Sui-Tang period, holding the pastures between the Songmo and the Huangshui rivers, bringing the Xi and Shiwei peoples under their influence, greatly increasing their herds of livestock and horses, and able to muster tens of thousands of riders in one stroke; that is the base of their manpower and their strength. Second, in the early Kaiyuan years the Tang tightened its management of the frontier prefectures, and the arrangements for jimi control, frontier trade, the purchase of horses and the state farms all shifted; the Khitan depended on the Tang for their markets and their titles, yet at the same time nursed grievances against the greed of the frontier officials, and any disturbance along the border was answered with a raid across the line. Third, the overall situation in the north was not relaxed in the second year of Kaiyuan; powers on the steppe were waxing and waning against one another, and the Khitan pushed south to probe, seeking grain, cattle and people in the gaps of the frontier defence. Judging from Dazuo Rong's situation, the expedition was clearly exploratory: he did not aim at taking walled towns, only at a success on the margins, which is why, when the Tang met him in ambush in the valley and broke the edge of his cavalry from the heights, the Khitan did not press the fight but gathered their men and fell back towards Yingzhou. The intelligence and the beacon relay of the Yingzhou circuit were the direct conditions that allowed the Tang to place the ambush at Lianshui Valley in good time; historians generally stress that it was precisely because the warning came in advance and because the river-valley terrain was used that a border trouble which might have spread was turned into a short, decisive engagement.
impact: 灤水谷之戰的影響，可以分對唐、對契丹、對北方格局三個層次來看。對唐廷而言，這是一場乾淨的邊防勝利：唐軍以極少傷亡的代價（史書未詳載我方損耗數）打退了契丹的大規模南進，保住了幽州與營州之間的交通與屯田區，也保住了唐廷對東北邊裔部族以羈縻待之的傳統姿態，讓契丹沒有藉口全面叛亂。這一戰也讓幽州長史兼安東都護薛耽的邊防聲望達到頂點，其後開元前期幽州換防與城障修築的政策，大致沿著這一役所確立的思路走，即以城塞為本、屯田為糧、伺隙而擊，而不與敵騎在平原上追逐消耗。對契丹而言，灤水谷的失利是一個沉重打擊：大祚榮本人在戰後退回營州，次年（開元三年）去世，弟咄吉嗣位；契丹在唐初的羈縻體系中原本只是眾多邊部之一，經此一敗，其內部整合加速，牙帳權力更趨集中，後來終於在安祿山、史思明叛亂前後，趁唐廷內亂大舉南下，長驅中原，完成從部族聯盟到跨區域帝國的跳躍。從更長的歷史看，此役也說明唐前期邊防的成色：當邊將得人、屯田有效、城防與烽燧連成線索時，數萬契丹騎兵確實可以被一場伏擊化為散沙；但當局面一旦被外亂打破，同樣的騎兵也能成為壓垮中原的洪流，這正是開元、天寶之間那道看不見的分水嶺。西北方面，此役雖無直接牽涉，但唐廷把主要精力放在北方與東北，也意味著安西與南疆的守備只能倚賴既有的都護府與軍鎮體系，資源分配的取捨由來伴隨著邊防的成敗。
impactEn: The effect of the Battle of Lianshui Valley can be read on three levels: for the Tang, for the Khitan, and for the shape of the north. To the Kaiyuan court it was a clean frontier victory: the Tang threw back a large Khitan incursion at very little cost in lives, for the histories do not record the Tang casualty figures, and in doing so preserved the communications and the farming lands between Youzhou and Yingzhou, and kept intact the Tang court's posture of treating the peoples of the north-east through the loose jimi system, so that the Khitan were given no pretext for open revolt. The battle also brought the frontier standing of Xue Dan, military prefect of Youzhou and Andong Protector, to its height; the policies that followed in the early Kaiyuan years for the rotation of garrisons and the repair of the wall-fortifications in Youzhou broadly followed the line established here, namely to take the fortified towns and the farms as the base, to strike when an opening appeared, and never to run exhausting races with enemy cavalry across the open plain. For the Khitan, the defeat at Lianshui Valley was a heavy blow: Dazuo Rong himself withdrew to Yingzhou and died the following year, 715, and his brother Duoji succeeded him. In the Tang's early system of jimi control the Khitan had been only one among many border peoples; after this defeat their internal integration accelerated, the authority of the central tent grew more concentrated, and in due course, amid the An Lushan and Shi Siming rebellions, taking advantage of the disorder in the Tang, they drove far into the north China plain and completed the leap from a tribal confederation to a transregional empire. Over the longer run the campaign also shows the quality of Tang frontier defence in its early phase: when the commanders were capable, the state farms worked and the walled towns and beacon towers formed a connected line, tens of thousands of Khitan riders could indeed be reduced to loose sand by a single ambush; but once the situation was broken by civil war, the same riders could become the flood that overwhelmed the central plains, and that is the invisible watershed between the Kaiyuan and Tianbao years. In the north-west the campaign was not directly involved, but the fact that the Tang devoted its main effort to the north and the north-east meant that the western regions and the southern frontier had to rely on the existing protectorates and garrison towns as they stood, and the choices in distributing resources had always come bundled with the successes and failures of frontier defence.
result: 結果是唐軍的決定性勝利，但並非戰略上的終局。開元二年夏秋之交，契丹大祚榮部在灤水谷被唐軍擊破：唐軍據險設伏，以長矛拒馬與弩箭控制谷口，待契丹騎兵入谷而無法展開時合擊兩翼，斬首數千級，俘獲一批部眾與馬匹，契丹殘部在失去統一指揮後各自散走，退出谷口，退回營州方向。唐軍隨即收兵回城，未作長距離追擊，理由是糧秣運補有限、秋季天氣轉冷，且深追入契丹牧地極易遭伏；此役之後，契丹在開元三年再攻邊，張守珪以安東都護之兵在累支山擊破之，開元四年更擒得其首領涅里，邊患才算暫時受控。大祚榮於開元三年去世，契丹由其子咄吉嗣位，唐廷仍以羈縻之策安撫，授官封爵、准其互市，以換取邊境的安寧，這一來一往的關係又延續了二十餘年，直到天寶年間形勢驟變。從兵器史的角度看，灤水谷之戰是長柄刺擊武器的一次實戰檢驗：卡面這件早王朝時期的埃及長矛早已退場三千年，但『金屬矛頭套合木杆』的做法，以及它在密集陣形中橫向攔截、逼退衝鋒騎兵的用法，都在這場戰鬥裡以唐軍的槊與長矛的形式延續了下來，成為冷兵器時代防禦騎兵最可靠的骨架之一。
resultEn: The result was a decisive Tang victory, but not a strategic conclusion. In the turn of summer and autumn of the second year of Kaiyuan, the Khitan under Dazuo Rong were broken at Lianshui Valley: the Tang held the heights, planted spear barriers and covered the mouth of the valley with crossbow fire, and when the Khitan riders had ridden in and could no longer deploy, they struck both flanks together and cut off the way back; several thousand heads were taken and a number of the enemy and their horses captured, while the broken Khitan units, having lost unified command, scattered and withdrew from the mouth of the valley back towards Yingzhou. The Tang then pulled back into the city without a long pursuit, for the grain could be brought up only so far, the autumn weather was turning cold, and a deep chase into Khitan pasture country invited ambush; after this the Khitan raided the border again in the third year of Kaiyuan, Zhang Shougui broke them at Leizhi Mountain with the troops of the Andong Protectorate, and in the fourth year he took their chief Nieli, and only then was the frontier trouble brought under control for a time. Dazuo Rong died in the third year of Kaiyuan, the Khitan were succeeded by his son Duoji, and the Tang court continued to soothe them with the jimi policy, granting offices and titles and permitting trade in exchange for peace on the frontier; that exchange of courtesies and grain lasted for more than twenty years, until the situation changed abruptly in the Tianbao years. From the point of view of the history of arms, the Battle of Lianshui Valley was a field test of the long-handled thrusting weapon: the Egyptian spear of the Early Dynastic period had left the scene three thousand years earlier, but the practice of a metal head socketed on a wooden shaft, and its use in dense formations to check a charge laterally and turn back charging horsemen, both continued in this fight in the form of the Tang sha and long spear, and became one of the most dependable frameworks of defence against cavalry in the age of cold weapons.
